doc.title: Betty Lee Hanson, Joe James, George Lewis, Joe Lewis, Joe Butler, Kid Thomas Valentine, Bill Russell, Allan Jaffe, Sandra Jaffe Interview, 1961-11-25
doc.interviewee: Betty Lee Hanson, Joe James, George Lewis, Joe Lewis, Joe Butler, Kid Thomas Valentine, Bill Russell, Allan Jaffe, Sandra Jaffe

title: Twenty bands, hiring leaders, and differences among them
summary: They hire leaders who bring their own players; over 20 bands and 160 musicians; Peter Bocage is more subdued than Kid Thomas.

story.theme_name: Leading a band: choosing, paying and managing players
story.community_name: Leading a band: running, choosing and keeping players

blocks.x: Well, did you find that you sort of got hold of a lot of extra musicians by word of mouth? Did they sort of come from the woods? Did they? Yes. Yes. I think we started out with just a few bands. In fact, when it first began, they were rotating a band once a week. And that's come to the point where we have over 20 bands and over 160 musicians that are just all seem to be falling into place. The orchestras and the bands are being more organized. At one time, a lot of the personnel were interchanging and taking their place with other leaders. But now, there is not very much of that unless a man happens to be away. Well, how do you get the bands? Do you organize the bands or do they organize themselves? No, they're organizing themselves. We've been hiring the leaders.

What we do is hire a person who is a leader, who had been a leader in the past. This is a person who is a leader musically and who knows the sound that he wants to produce from a band. He knows the other musicians and we hire a man, tell him to bring six pieces and he brings five musicians. Sometimes they're people we haven't heard before. A lot of times they're people we have heard before.

Were you able to discern which bands are better than others? I mean, do you sort of say to someone, thank you, we don't want you anymore? We haven't had to. In other words, they're all of a pretty good quality then.

Well, each band, as my wife said, there are 20 and each one is different. It's, the quality is certainly different. And I think the musical idea that the people are trying to get across is different also. There's range from Peter Boccage who plays a more subdued, a more quiet type music, quiet for jazz anyway. Maybe a little more sophisticated than a person, a kid Thomas. Yeah. Where a kid Thomas is, is a lot, maybe rougher, a lot more direct.
